import numpy as np, itertools, os,re
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); i=np.array(G['Demo pair 3 input']); o=np.array(G['Demo pair 3 output'])
pts=[(1,3),(3,0),(4,8)]
H,W=i.shape
def mind(p): return min(max(abs(p[0]-pr),abs(p[1]-pc)) for pr,pc in pts)
ch={(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if o[r][c]==5 and i[r][c]==1}
st={(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if o[r][c]==1 and i[r][c]==1}
# print dist map of changed cells to see structure
print('d ch:', sorted(set(mind(p) for p in ch)))
print('d st:', sorted(set(mind(p) for p in st)))
print('cheb d ch parity:',sorted(set(mind(p)%2 for p in ch)), 'st:',sorted(set(mind(p)%2 for p in st)))
# What distinguishes? maybe second-nearest cheb dist parity?
def sec(p): ds=sorted(max(abs(p[0]-pr),abs(p[1]-pc)) for pr,pc in pts); return ds[1]
print('ch sec:',Counter(sec(p) for p in ch))
print('st sec:',Counter(sec(p) for p in st))

import numpy as np, itertools, os,re
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load()
data=[]
for k in ['Demo pair 2','Demo pair 3','Demo pair 4','Demo pair 5','Demo pair 6']:
    i=np.array(G[k+' input']); o=np.array(G[k+' output'])
    H,W=i.shape
    pts=[(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if i[r][c]!=3]
    data.append((k,i,o,H,W,pts))
# For each bg cell, label changed(1)/kept(0). Feature: multiset {min-cheb dist to markers} vs kept.
import collections
rowsf=[]
for idx,(k,i,o,H,W,pts) in enumerate(data):
    for r in range(H):
        for c in range(W):
            if i[r][c]!=3: continue
            y=1 if o[r][c]==5 else 0
            ds=sorted(max(abs(r-pr),abs(c-pc)) for pr,pc in pts)
            rowsf.append((y,r,c,tuple(ds),idx,k,i[r][c]))
ch=[x for x in rowsf if x[0]==1]; st=[x for x in rowsf if x[0]==0]
# distribution of sorted-min-dist
print('changed min-ch dist:',collections.Counter(x[3][0] for x in ch))
print('kept min-ch dist:',collections.Counter(x[3][0] for x in st))

import numpy as np, collections, itertools, math, os,re
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load()
# Demo6: the visual pattern looked like a big X of thick diagonal strokes crossing the whole grid plus diamond outlines.
# Test new hypothesis: cell becomes 5 iff there exists a pair of markers such that cell lies BETWEEN them (strictly) on their straight line AND the cell's chebyshev-dist-to-nearest-marker is NOT smaller than distance-between-those-two-markers? Too complex; test simpler: cell lies strictly between two markers collinearly (already done: too few).
# Alternative: cell becomes 5 iff it lies on a line through TWO markers (infinite line), i.e., on any marker-line (not bounded to segment). Count coverage:
def lin(p,m): pass
for key in ['Demo pair 6','Demo pair 7']:
    ii=np.array(G[key+' input']); oo=np.array(G[key+' output'])
    H,W=ii.shape
    pts=[(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if ii[r][c]==1]
    ch={(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if ii[r][c]==6 and oo[r][c]==5}
    st={(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if ii[r][c]==6 and oo[r][c]==6}
    # on infinite line through >=2 markers
    al=set()
    for a,b in itertools.combinations(pts,2):
        dr=a[0]-b[0]; dc=a[1]-b[1]
        g=math.gcd(abs(dr),abs(dc))
        dr//=g; dc//=g
        rr,cc=a
        while 0<=rr<H and 0<=cc<W:
            al.add((rr,cc)); rr+=dr; cc+=dc
        rr,cc=b
        while 0<=rr<H and 0<=cc<W:
            al.add((rr,cc)); rr-=dr; cc-=dc
    print(key,'on-infinite-marker-lines: ch',len(ch&al),'/',len(ch),'st',len(st&al),'/',len(st))
